title.narrative: Second Kerala Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Project (Jalanidhi II)

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Kerala Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Project (Jalanidhi II) for India is to increase the access of rural communities to improved and sustainable water supply and sanitation services in Kerala, using a decentralized, demand-responsive approach. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is institution building. This component will: (i) support capacity building of sector institutions and support organizations; (ii) assist Government of Kerala (GOK) in implementing a statewide sector development program; and (iii) support project management costs. The second component of the project is technical assistance to implementing agencies. This component will provide technical assistance to implementing agencies such that the infrastructure investments under component three are properly implemented and the resultant services efficiently provided. The third component of the project is infrastructure development. This component will fund the implementation of infrastructure investments for: (i) new and rehabilitated intra-GP (Gram Panchayat) rural water supply schemes; (ii) pilot rehabilitation and modernization of multi-GP water supply schemes and transfer of internal distribution to GPs; and (iii) sanitation schemes, mainly covering community-centric solid and liquid waste management and household sanitation solutions in difficult terrain.

The development objective of the proposed project is to increase the access of rural communities to improved and sustainable water supply and sanitation services in Kerala, using a decentralized, demand-responsive approach.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :PASchedule, Section I .B.1 | Description :Kerala shall vest WRD with the responsibility for providing generaloversight and policy guidance to the Project, making any changes in the PIP, the Operational Manual, the Related Manuals and theSafeguards Instruments during implementation as may be needed, andapproving annual action plans and budgets prepared by KRWSA. |Frequency :Monthly

Finance Agreement :PASchedule, Section I .B.14 | Description :GOK shall, through KRWSA, ensure that: (a) the operationalmanagement and the financing responsibilities of selected existing single-GP Schemes and intra-GP parts of selected existingmulti-GP Schemes are transferred from KWA to the relevant Participating GP in accordance with an agreed time-bound action plan andschedule; (b) appropriate capital cost-sharing arrangements are implemented | Frequency :Monthly

Finance Agreement :PASchedule, Section I .B.16 | Description :KRWSA shall, consistent with a mutually agreed staffing plan,appoint within the PMU, the RPMUs and the GPSTs an adequate number ofstaff and external and internal auditor(s), with suitablequalifications and experience. | Frequency :Monthly

Finance Agreement :PASchedule, Section I .B.18 | Description :For the purpose of implementing the multi-GP Schemes, KRWSA shallenter into a tripartite MOU with KWA and Participating GPs. | Frequency :Monthly

Finance Agreement :PASchedule, Section I .B.2 | Description :Kerala and KRWSA shall carry out the Project in accordance with thePIP, the OM, the Related Manuals and the Safeguards Instruments. | Frequency :Monthly

Finance Agreement :PASchedule, Section I .B.3 | Description :Kerala shall appoint and maintain during the entire project durationan Executive Director at KRWSA to work on the Project on a full-time basis, and ensure that the tenure of any such ExecutiveDirector shall be for a period of not less than three years. | Frequency :Monthly

title.narrative: Number of GPs where interventions for safe disposal of solid and liquid waste successfully implemented and managed on a pilot basis

comment.narrative: <p>While the project could not develop any GP wide SLWM pilots, the project has supported 9652 small SLWM units covering 93 GPs benefitting 225,939 people, which showcased workable solutions for solid and liquid waste.</p>

title.narrative: Number of water utilities that the project is supporting

comment.narrative: <p>The project supported capacity-building of key technical staff of the KWA for rehabilitation of multi-GP schemes.</p>

title.narrative: Number of sector development studies successfully completed (cumulative)

comment.narrative: <p>10 studies completed against the target of nine studies.</p>

title.narrative: Piped household water connections that are benefiting from rehabilitation works undertaken by the project

comment.narrative: <p>92 percent of the revised target achieved. The original target was split into a sub indicator to show new and rehabilitation works connections separately. Achieved 102 percent targets against the indicator on new schemes.</p>

title.narrative: Number of people in rural areas provided with access to Improved Water Sources under the project

comment.narrative: <p>100 percent of the original target and 84 percent of the revised target achieved. Out of 1,157,000 people provided with access, 1,154,750 people used the water supply,  as some flood affected connections were yet to be restored by closing.</p>

<p>84 percent of the original target and 89 percent of the revised target achieved . The  target could not be fully achieved as two large multi-GP schemes were dropped due to the fall in the dollar against SDR and increased costs.</p>

title.narrative: Total number of new water supply schemes being operated (cumulative)

comment.narrative: <p>96 percent of the target achieved. This is a revised indicator. The original indicator  included both new and rehabilitated schemes together with a target of 3938. The restructuring in 2016 split it into two indicators with a target of 1775 for new schemes and 400 for rehabilitated schemes</p>

title.narrative: Number of water supply schemes improved under the project that are delivering satisfactory services to all intended households by recovering full operational costs

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement exceeded the target (104 percent). This is a revised  indicator , as per the restructuring in June 2016, in place of  " Number of operational water schemes for which KRWSA's sustainability index is >80% " , which had a target of 3150 schemes.</p>

title.narrative: Number of project supported water supply schemes that are managed by beneficiary groups following demand responsive approach

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. This is a revised  indicator , as per the restructuring in June 2016, in place of  " Numberof GPs in the State that are implementing decentralized, demand responsive projects in RWSS", which had a target of 200 GPs.</p>

title.narrative: Number of project supported multi-Gram Panchayat schemes by local institutions successfully demonstrated improved service delivery

comment.narrative: <p>Three of the five targeted schemes completed. This is a revision of the original indicator " Total number of multi-GP schemes partially transferred to GPs and rehabilitated/ modernized (cumulative number of GPs benefited)"  with a target of 15 GPs. The project has completed  three multi GP schemes,  covering 12 GPs. Two multi-GP schemes were dropped due to the fall in the dollar against SDR and increased costs</p>

title.narrative: Number of other water service providers that the project is supporting

comment.narrative: <p>76 percent of the target achieved. While only 3,578 BGs received technical assistance for RWSS against the target of 4713, the number of households per BG were more. While it was planned to cover 225, 891 households from 200 GPs, the project covered 258,417 households from 115 GPs.</p>

title.narrative: Improved latrines constructed under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievements exceeded the targets considerably (363 percent), because the State focused more on achieving the ODF status in order to align with the priorities of the  SBM</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to "improved sanitation facilities under the proj.

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement exceeded (105 percent) the revised target. The original target was reduced by half, due to modification in the project scope.</p>

title.narrative: Number of project GPs benefiting from technical assistance and capacity building (cumulative)

comment.narrative: <p>The achievement exceeded the target considerably (199 percent of the revised target),  because the  project supported the <em>Suchithwa Mission</em> by providing 84 resource persons in project districts covering 598 GPs to conduct a behavioral change campaign, which was not originally envisaged.</p>

title.narrative: Number of capacity building traning events carried out (cumulative)

comment.narrative: <p>94 percent of the revised target achieved.8,546 capacity development events covered  627,394 person-days</p>
